card.title: Exam bank — every board question on quantity of heat

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Three questions: aluminium block heating (2024: 200 g, 20 to 100 C absorbs 14,400 J), latent fusion vs vaporization distinction (2023), Q and c definitions plus warming formula (2023). Sensible heat warms (mc dT); latent heat transforms (mL) at fixed temperature.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Q = m c dT (c: J/kg K) · Q = m L (fusion/vaporization, J/kg) · mixture: lost = gained · cooling dT/dt = -k(T - T0)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: mc dT needs no phase change inside the interval (meaning c roughly constant). Latent formulas need constant pressure at the transition point. Mixture ledgers assume isolated calorimeters. Newton cooling needs small excess temperature.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 200 g Al: 0.2 x 900 x 80 = 14,400 J. Fusion breaks lattice (3.34x10^5 J/kg ice); vaporization breaks all bonds (2.26x10^6 J/kg steam — why steam scalds worse). Triple point: all three phases coexist at one (P,T).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: NEB 2024 (3): Q = 0.2 x 900 x 80 = 14,400 J absorbed. NEB 2023 (3): fusion melts solids at fixed T, vaporization boils liquids at fixed T — both Q = mL with no thermometer movement. NEB 2023 (3): Q defined as transit energy, c as per-kg-per-kelvin cost, formula Q = mc dT.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mark-losers: grams left unconverted (200 g = 0.2 kg); dT applied across phase changes; c treated constant over huge ranges. Latent heat vanishes at the critical point.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Mixture method: hot ledger equals cold ledger (plus calorimeter term) — solve for unknown c. Latent measurement runs the same ledger with one side mL. Cooling integrates to exponential decay.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Warming vs changing phase decides mc dT vs mL — read the verb (heats/melts/boils). Mixture: lost = gained first line. Triple point: one sentence (three phases, one point).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2024 (3): Al block heating numerical. NEB 2023 (3): fusion vs vaporization latent. NEB 2023 (3): Q/c definitions + warming formula.
